result: The study enrolled two cohorts of healthy young adults (ages 18-40) of Caucasian ancestry: 119 males (discovery cohort) and 128 females (validation cohort). Both cohorts received trivalent influenza vaccine and underwent longitudinal sampling for genotyping (730,525 SNPs), gene expression (9,809 transcripts at days 0, 1, 3, 14), and antibody titers (days 0, 14, 28). Quality control procedures included exclusion of individuals with missing data, SNP filtering (MAF>0.05, HWE p>0.001), and removal of population outliers.
status_reasoning: Claims C11-C52, C85-C87 collectively describe a well-designed longitudinal study with appropriate sample sizes, clear inclusion/exclusion criteria, validated technical platforms, and rigorous quality control procedures. The use of sex-stratified discovery and validation cohorts, standardized sample collection protocols, and comprehensive quality metrics (call rates >0.99, detection thresholds, batch processing controls) support the methodological rigor of the study design.

result: 78 genes showed both significant genotype-expression association (eQTL) and transcriptional response to vaccination in both cohorts. At some loci, the magnitude of genetic effects on expression changed after vaccination, with increased effect size (slope) being the main driver rather than decreased within-genotype variance. 146 SNP-transcript pairs in the top 1% of delta-R²g distribution with strong cis-eQTL (p<5×10⁻⁸) were identified, and delta-R²g values showed consistency between cohorts (Spearman correlation=0.25, p<2×10⁻¹⁶).

The analysis of temporal changes in genetic effects (delta-R²g) is methodologically sound, using variance decomposition to identify that effect size changes rather than variance changes drive the observed patterns. The significant correlation between cohorts (C53) provides validation, though the modest correlation coefficient (0.25) suggests some heterogeneity.

result: Content analysis of 98 genes with strong eQTL and vaccine response showed significant enrichment for genes involved in antigen processing and presentation, cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-mediated apoptosis, dendritic cell function, and membrane trafficking. Seven of the 20 genes with strongest integrative evidence are involved in intracellular antigen transport, processing, and presentation. Many identified genes encode proteins with general roles in membrane trafficking rather than immune-specific functions.

result: 301 genes showed significant correlation between gene expression and antibody response in both cohorts (281 positive, 83 negative correlations). Individual responses to the three viral antigens were correlated within individuals. A Titer Response Index (TRI) was computed to integrate responses across vaccine components while accounting for pre-vaccination titers. Genes were selected using F-statistic p<0.01 and maximum average correlation >0.15 between cohorts.

The power properties for reactive and causal model tests are equivalent due to symmetric model structures.

result: The study has several acknowledged limitations: restriction to healthy young adults (excluding children, elderly, severely ill); ethnically homogeneous population to minimize stratification; insufficient sample size to establish causal relationships between identified loci and antibody response; and use of antibody titers that do not capture full immune response complexity. Additional studies are needed to validate findings in other populations, establish causality, and examine cell-mediated immunity.
